name: دوران قيم القائمة الى اليسار بمقدار موضع واحد
description: انشاء برنامج يحتوي على دالة تستقبل قائمة من القيم وتعيد القائمة بعد تدويرها الى اليسار بمقدار موضع واحد بحيث تنتقل القيمة الموجودة في بداية القائمة الى نهايتها ويظل ترتيب القيم الاخرى كما هو. على سبيل المثال، اذا كانت القائمة [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]، فسيتم تغييرها الى [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 1].
code:
#Khatwa 1: Ta3reef al-dala
def rotate_left(lst):
    #Khatwa 1.1: Khazan al-qimma al-oola fi mutaghayyar mahalli
    first = lst[0] 
    #Khatwa 1.2: Dawwir al-baqi min al-qiyam ila al-yasar
    for i in range(len(lst)-1):
        lst[i] = lst[i + 1]
    #Khatwa 1.3: Naql al-qimma al-oola ila nihayat al-qaimah
    lst[len(lst)-1] = first    
    return lst
#Khatwa 2: Nadi al-dala
values =  [3, 8, 9, 8, 7, 5]
print("al-qaimah al-asliya:", values)
print("al-qaimah al-mudawara: ", rotate_left(values))

untr_comments.content:
With value at the front safely tucked away, we now have to shift the remaining values to the left by one position. We could break down the overall task into shifting operations, each of which is a simple assignment statement.

Because of repeated shift operations on the list elements, we’d want to write this with a for loop. We’ll replace the element at index i with the value currently stored in the element at index i+1, this will shift the value at index i+1 to the left, by one position.

Note that, instead of range(len(lst)), we need to use range(len(lst)-1)). The reason is that in the assignment statement in the loop body we always move the element one position ahead of the element at the current index. So, to shift all the remaining elements, we need to iterate through indexes that start at 0 with every integer number up to but not including len(lst)-1.
Note that len(lst) returns the number of the values in the list. Also, note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header.

untr_name: Rotating the List Values to the Left by One Position
untr_description: Construct a program that has a function that receives a list of values and returns the list rotated to the left by 1 position so that the value at the front of the list goes to the back and the order of the other values stays the same. For example, if the list is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], the program will change it to [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 1].
untr_code:
#Step 1: Define the function
def rotate_left(lst):
    #Step 1.1: Store the value at the front in a local variable
    first = lst[0] 
    #Step 1.2: Rotate the remaining values of the list to the left 
    for i in range(len(lst)-1):
        lst[i] = lst[i + 1]
    #Step 1.3: Move the value at the front to the back of the list
    lst[len(lst)-1] = first    
    return lst
#Step 2: Call the function
values =  [3, 8, 9, 8, 7, 5]
print("Original list:", values)
print("Rotated list: ", rotate_left(values))
